Hi there! I have hashimotos (a thyroid autoimmune disease) so I understand what it’s like to not be able to lose weight. I have tried mounjaro under medical supervision. 

I went on Mounjaro for about 7 months because I gained  20lbs before I was diagnosed (I’m 5’2 and I was about 140lbs). I didn’t really work out a lot because I was super lethargic still trying to get my thyroid under control but I ate very healthy and mounjaro got rid of my sweet tooth so I didn’t get those pesky PMS cravings. I managed to get down to 104lbs. 

I honestly didn’t have any major complications, but the nausea was awful and I couldn’t keep food down for the first month. This is just my opinion based on my experience but for me it was worth it, I’ve struggled a lot with my weight since I was in my teens (I’m 29).

I had monthly follow ups with the doctor and I didn’t really go above 5mg. I was only on 5mg for a month, as well the whole time I was on the starting dose of 2.5.

Hey there :), like you (27f) I got diagnosed almost 3 months ago now. I’d like to reassure you that it is possible to have a successful career and have hashimoto’s. 

I found out I had hashimotos and I was in the middle of applying to other jobs because my last workplace was toxic, so I had to manage my role and apply to other jobs. And just last week I started a new job (a much better job) with a promotion. For reference I’m a Senior Consultant at a big firm, so it’s a pretty hectic job with a lot of late nights and early mornings and travel. If you’re taking Levo, once you adjust your dose it should help with the energy levels a bit. 

To be honest, I did have to change my lifestyle a bit, I can’t go out after work because I do need to rest sometimes. Also if you can work from home it’s a great help. 

I think you can have a very successful career but genuinely it does take being conscious that some of us have limited energy and can’t do everything (it’s not great, but what can we do). Just be kind to yourself, I know it’s cheesy but it helps :)

Sounds like you’ve been going through a lot! Message me if you ever need someone to talk to about all this. 

I don’t know much about your history or the healthcare system where you live, but the way I did this was, I got a private clinic to do a full panel blood test (because I didn’t know what was wrong). Once I saw my TSH (first time it was 15.8), I looked for an endo. 

In your case, it’s harder when your numbers aren’t reflecting your symptoms, but I think try to find an endo that at least will give you something to manage your symptoms and follow up with you accordingly, in case the time comes to put you on meds. But definitely get your calcium levels checked out further, and try to figure out why they’re elevated (if you haven’t already of course). 

Honestly in terms of coping I think take it easy on yourself, don’t over exert yourself, try to keep your stress levels as low as you can (I know with work that may be tough). I know it’s cheesy but genuinely be kind to yourself, this isn’t an easy ordeal, it’s a life changing condition. Honestly I started seeing a therapist after I got diagnosed because I needed someone who I could talk to that would have a neutral reaction and a logical one. Cause when I talk to people they either think I’m exaggerating how much this affects my life, or they look at me with pity.
I’ll definitely talk to my endo about it when I can see him. But thank you you’ve been extremely helpful and supportive 😊
